title: P0 Hosted API - session splay and KV throb diagnostic
content:
Summary:

On 2029-06-14 03:42 UTC we observed a P0 degradation of the Hosted API for ~1.5 hours that manifested primarily as elevated p95/p99 generation latency and intermittent streaming session resets. The incident was driven by a correlated pattern we are calling a 'session splay' — a wide skew in session start times across the edge fleet — that amplified KV cache pressure and led to a 'KV throb' (periodic spikes in KV mutex latency and transient lease contention).

Impact:
- Duration: ~03:42 UTC -> 05:12 UTC (region: us-west1 primarily).
- Symptoms: p95 generation latency rose from baseline ~200ms to 1.2s; p99 spiked up to 3.6s.
- Streaming: ~12% of streaming sessions experienced early termination or reconnects during the peak window.
- Error rates: 5xx increased from 0.2% to 1.4% (short-lived).
- Customer visible: increased latency, some reconnects, marginally increased token cost due to retries. No data loss reported.

Detection and Pager Timeline (high-level):
- 03:41 UTC: synthetic round-trip p95 alert (hosted-api-p95-rt) fires.
- 03:42 UTC: SRE on-call (Evan) paged. Initial dashboard shows region-localized spike in p95 and streaming session churn.
- 03:45 UTC: Triage: edge-aggregation metrics show large number of sessions starting in a ~60s window into a small subset of edge pods.
- 03:50 UTC: Correlation to KV backend: kv-latency-avg increased; lock wait time metrics show periodic spikes.
- 04:05 UTC: Mitigation: temporary traffic re-route to secondary region for high-RT customers and increase KV read replicas for impacted cache shard.
- 04:18 UTC: Observed latency improvement on routed traffic; reconnect rate begins to fall.
- 05:10 UTC: Post-mitigation validation; traffic normalized.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
A combination of an upstream client-side rollout (non-Redwood SDK) and an unfortunate timing of ephemeral client reconnects produced many session-start events concentrated within small time windows across several edge POPs. The serving edge attempted to populate KV-prefetch entries simultaneously for those sessions, which overloaded a small number of KV shard leaders. The KV leader nodes experienced mutex/lease contention and GC pressure on the metadata store which introduced tail latency spikes. Those KV tail spikes cascaded back to the serving runtime: token generation tasks that needed prefix/KV data stalled waiting on locks, increasing p95/p99 and causing streaming reassembly timeouts.

Contributing factors:
- Edge session scheduler uses a heuristic that can cluster session allocation when bursty connections arrive (scheduler splay mis-calibrated).
- KV shard assignment placed many new sessions onto the same small leader set due to recent rebalancer churn (rebalance job ran ~10m before incident).
- Insufficient soft throttling on session-creation code path (we eagerly prefetch heavy blobs for every new session).
- Monitoring threshold configuration: kv-lock-waits alert had slow burn threshold and did not trigger early enough.
- A client-side rollout (3rd-party integrator) that introduced aggressive reconnect backoff jitter being effectively zero for some clients; this amplified clustering.

Immediate mitigations taken during the incident:
- Reroute: applied region-based routing fallback for high-latency customers to reduce load concentration on us-west1. (owner: NetOps, actioned 04:05 UTC).
- Hotscale: spun extra KV read-replicas and promoted two follower nodes for the affected shards, reducing leader CPU and lock wait. (owner: infra-kv, 04:10 UTC).
- Temp throttle: deployed a hotfix to session creation path to limit parallel prefetches per edge pod (soft cap to 8 prefetch ops). (owner: serving-runtime, 04:20 UTC).
- Rolling back a prior aggressive rebalancer config that increased shard stickiness; reverted to previous stable config to re-spread session assignment. (owner: infra-kv, 04:32 UTC).

Why mitigations worked:
- Rerouting immediately reduced the load density in the hot POPs and lowered the number of near-simultaneous session starts.
- Increasing KV replica count and demoting overloaded leaders reduced contention and lowered lock wait percentiles.
- Soft-throttling prefetches decreased bursty IO to KV and prevented surge amplification.

Post-incident analysis and data (highlights):
- KV lock wait p99 timeline aligned with p99 generation latency within a 30–40s window.
- Edge scheduler logs show >3x normal session-starts in 60s windows for ~7 pods.
- Rebalancer telemetry indicates a rebalance completed 9m before incident start; that job had a shorter stabilization window configured during last deploy.
- Client-side logs from a partner show reconnect jitter set to 0–1s (no exponential backoff) for a subset of SDK versions.

Runbook draft (actions to take when similar symptoms observed):
1) Immediate triage steps:
   - Check hosted-api-p95 and streaming-reconnect dashboards.
   - Query edge-session-start-rate for top POPs in last 2m window. If any POP shows >2x baseline concentrated starts, continue.
   - Inspect kv-lock-wait p95/p99 for implicated shards.
2) Short-term mitigations:
   - Apply region routing failover for affected customer routes (NetOps).
   - Hotscale KV replicas for the implicated shard (infra-kv).
   - Push temporary session-prefetch cap (serving-runtime) to reduce parallel KV ops.
3) Safety rollbacks:
   - Rollback any rebalancer config changes from the last 15m if timing aligns with spike.
4) Communication:
   - Post initial Slack incident channel summary, include affected regions/customers and ETA for mitigation.

Monitoring and alerting changes proposed:
- New synthetic: edge-session-start-burst detector (alert if >X starts in Y seconds per POP).
- Lower kv-lock-wait alert threshold to detect faster (shorter burn) when p95 crosses baseline + N sigma.
- Add correlation alert that fires when session-start-burst AND kv-lock-wait p95 rise within 60s.
- Add dashboard showing rebalance-job-run timestamps against session-start heatmap for quick correlation.

Longer-term remediation plans (owners + rough ETA):
- Scheduler splay redesign (eng-serving-runtime): rework allocation heuristic to spread new sessions across pods with randomized start windows. ETA: 6 weeks. (owner: Priya Nair)
- Staggered prefetch strategy (eng-serving-runtime): introduce low-priority background prefetch with immediate-on-demand hot-path. ETA: 4 weeks. (owner: Owen Rodriguez)
- Rebalancer safety: add safety window and slow-down on rebalance during peak traffic hours; add canary limits. ETA: 3 weeks. (owner: infra-kv)
- Client outreach: notify partner engineering teams about observed bad reconnect jitter; add to partner integration guide and release notes. ETA: 2 weeks (owner: Customer Success / Solutions Eng)
- KV leader autoscale and leader-fanout improvements: explore automatic leader offloading when lock waits exceed threshold. ETA: 8 weeks. (owner: infra-kv)

Postmortem action items (tracked):
- ACTION-1: Implement edge-session-start-burst synthetic (owner: SRE monitoring, ETA: 2w).
- ACTION-2: Deploy temporary kv-lock-wait fast alert rule (owner: infra-kv, ETA: 3d).
- ACTION-3: Create backstop policy to cap prefetch concurrency on session creation (owner: serving-runtime, ETA: 1w).
- ACTION-4: Add rebalance run metadata to main monitoring plane (owner: infra-kv, ETA: 2w).
- ACTION-5: Run chaos test that simulates high-frequency reconnects to validate splay and prefetch cap (owner: eng-sre + QA, ETA: 4w).

Open questions and unresolved items:
- Was there any cascading effect from tenant-level rate limiting that we didn't capture? Need cost-accounting check.
- Can we identify exact client versions that caused the zero-jitter reconnects? Solutions Eng to follow up.
- Are there KV metadata GC knobs we should tune to avoid transient GC during leader churn? infra-kv to investigate.

Lessons learned (brief):
- Bursty session starts are a first-class failure mode for systems with eager prefetch and centralized metadata stores.
- Rapid rebalancer changes near traffic peaks are risky; we need more conservative defaults and better observability tying rebalance to session heatmaps.
- Small client-side misconfigurations can amplify infra-level weaknesses; partner integrations need clear backoff expectations.

Appendix (useful queries / dashboards):
- edge-session-start-rate by POP (1m/5m/15m).
- kv-lock-wait p50/p95/p99 by shard and node.
- rebalance-job history (start/complete timestamps).
- streaming-session-reconnects by POP and edge-pod.
- top-10 pods by session-start-concentration.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is a working draft. Please add missing telemetry links and correct owner assignments if needed. The immediate temp mitigations are already in prod; action items need triage into the SRE board.

-- Evan
